units.title: Epic and Drama
units.blurb: Homer's two epics and the playwrights of Athens, who invented tragedy and comedy.

units.title: The First Historians
units.blurb: Herodotus and Thucydides, who first tried to find out what happened and why.

units.title: Plato
units.blurb: Socrates' questions, written down by his student: justice, knowledge, love and the soul.

units.title: Aristotle
units.blurb: Logic, nature, the soul, ethics, politics and poetry from the philosopher who tried to study everything.

units.title: Medicine and Mathematics
units.blurb: Hippocrates' medicine, Euclid's geometry and Archimedes' mechanics.

topics.title: Homer: The Iliad
topics.short: The anger of Achilles in the last year of the Trojan War, and what it costs Greeks and Trojans alike.

topics.title: Homer: The Odyssey
topics.short: Odysseus' ten-year voyage home from Troy, and his wife and son holding out for him in Ithaca.

topics.title: Aeschylus: The Oresteia
topics.short: A family curse runs through three plays and ends in a court of law: revenge gives way to justice.

topics.title: Sophocles: Oedipus and Antigone
topics.short: A king hunts for the cause of a plague and finds himself; his daughter defies a king to bury her brother.

topics.title: Euripides: The Plays
topics.short: The most questioning of the three tragedians: war's victims, passion and the gods seen from below.

topics.title: Aristophanes: The Comedies
topics.short: Wild comic fantasies that poke fun at Athens' leaders, poets and philosophers, Socrates included.

topics.title: Herodotus: The Histories
topics.short: The first great history: why Greeks and Persians went to war, with every story he heard along the way.

topics.title: Thucydides: The Peloponnesian War
topics.short: An Athenian general's careful account of the long war between Athens and Sparta, and of power without limits.

topics.title: Plato: The Trial of Socrates
topics.short: Socrates questions a man about holiness, defends his life before a jury, and refuses to escape from prison.

topics.title: Plato: Phaedo
topics.short: Socrates' last day: a conversation about whether the soul outlives the body.

topics.title: Plato: Meno
topics.short: Can virtue be taught? Socrates helps a boy discover a geometry fact he was never told.

topics.title: Plato: Protagoras and Gorgias
topics.short: Socrates against the teachers of persuasion: is it better to suffer wrong than to do it?

topics.title: Plato: Symposium and Phaedrus
topics.short: Speeches at a dinner party on love, climbing from love of one person to love of beauty itself.

topics.title: Plato: The Republic, Books I–V
topics.short: What is justice? Socrates builds a city in words to find out, then looks for justice in the soul.

topics.title: Plato: The Republic, Books VI–X
topics.short: The philosopher-ruler, the divided line, the cave, how cities decline, and the myth of Er.

topics.title: Plato: Theaetetus and Sophist
topics.short: What is knowledge? A young mathematician tries three answers, and Socrates tests each one.

topics.title: Plato: Timaeus and Critias
topics.short: A likely story of how the world was made from shapes and numbers, and the tale of Atlantis.

topics.title: Plato: Statesman, Laws and the Seventh Letter
topics.short: Plato's last thoughts on ruling and on laws for a real city, and his own story of politics in Sicily.

topics.title: Aristotle: Logic
topics.short: The first full study of reasoning: the syllogism, proof, argument and the tricks of false arguments.

topics.title: Aristotle: Physics
topics.short: Nature, change and its four kinds of cause, place, time, the infinite and the unmoved mover.

topics.title: Aristotle: On the Heavens
topics.short: A round Earth at the center of perfect spheres, the four elements, and weather, comets and rainbows.

topics.title: Aristotle: On the Soul
topics.short: The soul as what makes a living body alive, from plants to people, and how we sense, remember and think.

topics.title: Aristotle: Metaphysics
topics.short: The study of being as being: substance, form and matter, and the first cause of all motion.

topics.title: Aristotle: The Animals
topics.short: The first great work of biology: careful observation of hundreds of animals, and why their parts are as they are.

topics.title: Aristotle: Nicomachean Ethics
topics.short: Happiness as a life of virtue, virtue as a habit between two extremes, and why friends matter.

topics.title: Aristotle: Politics
topics.short: Humans as political animals, the kinds of constitution, and what makes a city good and stable.

topics.title: Aristotle: Rhetoric and Poetics
topics.short: How persuasion works, and what makes a tragedy move us: plot, character and the turn of fortune.

topics.title: Hippocrates: On Medicine
topics.short: Medicine that looks for natural causes, watches the patient closely, and aims to help, or at least to do no harm.

topics.title: Euclid: Elements, Books I–IV
topics.short: Definitions, postulates and proofs: triangles, parallels, the Pythagorean theorem and circles.

topics.title: Euclid: Elements, Books V–X
topics.short: Ratio and proportion, similar figures, prime numbers, the infinitude of primes and incommensurable lengths.

topics.title: Euclid: Elements, Books XI–XIII
topics.short: Solid geometry, the method of exhaustion, and the five regular solids.

topics.title: Archimedes: The Works
topics.short: The law of the lever, why things float, pi trapped between two bounds, and counting the grains of sand to fill the universe.
